thread:
maria: Quick Q — there was a convo last week about model selection semantics. If a client sends both model_id and routing_hint in the same request, which wins? We have customers depending on older SDKs that only set routing_hint.
kevin: Currently code path is: if model_id present -> strict pick, else if routing_hint present -> choose best model for hint (may return different model ids). But that's actually an implementation detail, not contract. We need to make this explicit in the API docs.
song: Agree we should lock the behavior. Proposal: model_id is authoritative. routing_hint is only advisory when model_id is missing. Falls back to per-region tier mapping.
jenna: That seems fine, but we need to call out backward compatibility: older SDKs that used `routing_hint: "preferred:gptx"` should continue to work. Also want to ensure responses include `model_selected` in the response envelope so clients can audit.
maria: Adding to that — what about fallback ordering? If routing_hint maps to a list of compatible models, are we allowed to return any compatible model or must we follow a deterministic priority list?
kevin: Deterministic priority is required for reproducibility. The runtime will pick the highest-priority compatible model for the (region,tier) bucket. If capacity constraints force a different one, we add `fallback_reason` in response. Example: `fallback_reason: "capacity:region-us-west:primary-unavailable"`.
jenna: For the response envelope schema, suggest adding these fields (all optional): `model_selected`, `model_version`, `fallback_reason`, `routing_hint_used` so telemetry and customer code can detect changes.
maria: OK. Code review ping — @kevin can you add those fields to the API spec and OpenAPI file? Small sample of how clients will see it: ```json
{  "id":"resp_123","model_selected":"redwood-gpt-3.2","model_version":"3.2.1","fallback_reason":"capacity:region-us-west:primary-unavailable","usage":{"tokens":45},"output":"..."}
```
rollout-bot: Scheduled rollout checklist created: /rollouts/region-routing-2026-03 — canary starts 2026-03-25 10:00 UTC.
song: One more edge: what if client sends `model_hint_list` (array) for backwards compat? We currently accept `routing_hint` string or `model_hint_list` in body. Should we deprecate `model_hint_list`?
kevin: Let's not break customers. Mark `model_hint_list` deprecated in schema but accept it until end of quarter. Server will treat it as equivalent to an ordered `routing_hint` list — translate to internal priority list. Add deprecation notice in docs and telemetry tag `deprecated_hint_used`.
jenna: Tests: add contract tests for combinations: (1) model_id+routing_hint, (2) routing_hint only, (3) model_hint_list only, (4) invalid model_id with routing_hint. These should assert presence/absence of `fallback_reason` and `model_selected`.
maria: Thanks. Action items: @kevin update OpenAPI + jsonschema, @song add runtime guard for deterministic priority + telemetry hooks, @jenna add contract tests and eval prompt to detect output regressions when fallback happens. I'll follow up on the rollout doc.
kevin: Will do — PR incoming today, ping for review.
song: I'll add a small smoke check in the canary to surface `deprecated_hint_used` metric.
maria: Cool. If anyone hits a customer bug related to ambiguous selection, escalate to this thread and link the rollout doc. :thumbsup:
